summary.text: A 76-year-old man with high blood pressure, atrial fibrillation and type 2 diabetes underwent suboccipital craniectomy for evacuation of a posterior fossa hematoma, with uneventful recovery and discharge home.

He was readmitted 19 days later with fever of 39°C, neck stiffness, photophobia, altered consciousness (Glasgow Coma Scale 10) and necrosis of the upper third of the surgical wound with purulent discharge.

Workup showed leukocytosis, raised C-reactive protein and procalcitonin, an organizing collection with a fistulous tract to the skin on CT, and CSF findings consistent with bacterial meningitis; blood cultures were negative.
He underwent wound debridement and skin closure, was started on ceftazidime and linezolid and admitted to neurosurgical intensive care on mechanical ventilation and sedation.
Intraoperative samples grew carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (likely KPC) sensitive only to colistin and fosfomycin, and treatment was changed to colistin and fosfomycin.
Neurological improvement followed, repeat CSF on postoperative day 8 showed sterilization and follow-up CT showed the collection had disappeared.
On postoperative day 12 he developed acute respiratory distress and hemodynamic collapse, a massive pulmonary embolism was diagnosed despite enoxaparin prophylaxis, and he died despite resuscitation.

ambiguities.issue: Postoperative-day numbering uses different, unstated reference surgeries: day 19 follows the index craniectomy, whereas days 6, 8 and 12 are not explicitly anchored (the abstract says death 12 days after surgical revision).
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assume the anchor for days 6, 8 and 12 beyond the literal text, and do not compute calendar intervals.

evidence.quote: Surgical revision revealed a collection fistulized to the skin.
The patient was urgently taken to the operating room for wound debridement and skin closure.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract names a surgical revision and the case text a wound debridement and skin closure; the source does not state that they are the same operation.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not merge the two operations or assign the abstract finding to the debridement.

evidence.quote: On admission, the patient was screened for MDR organisms as per hospital protocol.

ambiguities.issue: It is not stated whether "On admission" refers to the index admission or the readmission.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign the screening to a specific admission.

evidence.quote: Five days after surgery, we received cultures results: intraoperative samples were positive for K. pneumoniae producing carbapenemase (likely KPC), showing sensitivity only to colistin and fosfomycin [Table 1].
Table 1: Antibiogram.

ambiguities.issue: Table 1 (antibiogram) exists only as an image; its cells are not quotable source text, so no per-antibiotic facts are extracted. Carbapenemase type is only "likely KPC".
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not extract per-antibiotic results or a confirmed carbapenemase type from the narrative.

evidence.quote: In our case, although susceptibility to agents such as meropenem-vaborbactam or cefiderocol was likely, these antimicrobials were not available in our institution at the time of treatment.

ambiguities.issue: Susceptibility to meropenem-vaborbactam or cefiderocol is described as likely, not tested; these drugs were not given.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record these agents as tested, susceptible or administered.

evidence.quote: These factors likely contributed to the development of a nosocomial infection with an XDR organism.
The patient had multiple risk factors for thromboembolism, including recent major neurosurgery, prolonged immobilization, systemic inflammation, and critical illness.

ambiguities.issue: Authors hedge the nosocomial origin ("likely", "suggests") and attribute thromboembolic risk factors by interpretation, not as separately documented findings.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record nosocomial acquisition, prolonged immobilization or critical illness as confirmed conditions.

evidence.quote: Five days after surgery, we received cultures results

Neurological improvement was observed 48 h after changing the treatment (BIS between 60 and 70, localized motor response to pain, eye opening to stimulation), corresponding to the 6^(th) postoperative day.

ambiguities.issue: Culture results arrived five days after surgery, yet improvement 48 h after the treatment change is placed on postoperative day 6, which would put the change before the reported culture results; the narrative implies the change followed the results.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not fix a calendar day for the switch to colistin and fosfomycin or order it against the culture report.
